source: Graduale Romanum 1961 textus novus pp.143** and 144**, first verses notated; all four subsequent full verses are unnotated in source
editorCaution: These four scores are deliberately musical SCHEMATICS, not source-backed complete transcriptions. Exsurge parsing is purely typographical. Every difficult medial accent/secondary accent needs a Gregorian editor with the primary 1961 score and Solesmes rulebook. Do not auto-merge.

sourceLatin: Dóminus exercítuum: ipse est rex glóriae.
sourceSyllables: Dó-mi-nus ex-er-cí-tu-um: ip-se est rex gló-ri-ae.
cases.medialTonicPitchCell: initial h tenor; first accented motif (ixi or ixi hr) then second motif g or g hr
cases.hypothesisWhyNotMusicallyCertified: Two adjacent lexical accents rex glóriae are not source-notated as a later-verse mediant; combining the first-verse 23 tonic cell with the dactylic expansion seen in Psalm46 is hypothetical
cases.gabcPunctuationCaveat: Colon after exercítuum is printed source punctuation, omitted from lyric string in this research GABC: the correct musical pause/rest/halfbar has NOT been chosen, and this research-only rendering must not be taken as liturgically correctly punctuated.
